title: Attachment
description: Discover the liberating power of non-attachment, learning how to engage fully with life without being bound by expectations or cravings.

sutra.meaning: Mind becomes calm by detachment or contemplation on realised sages

sections.insight: Letting go brings peace or complete focus on each posture and each breath.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I able to maintain focus?
sections.practice: Observe yourself whenever you feel attachment and possesiveness to people and objects.

sutra.meaning: Suffering comes from 1. ignorance or lack of wisdom, 2.ego, 3.attachment to pleasure, 4.aversion to pain and 5.fear of death. These are the root causes of disturbance in our equilibrium.

sections.insight: All sufferings have one or the other of these at its root.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I see their presence in me?
sections.practice: Recall incidents causing you distress and identify the reason at their root. Identify one pattern.
sections.journalPrompt: What did I find at the root?
sections.shlokaFrom: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी॥ 2.70
sections.wisdomFrom: A person who is not disturbed by the incessant flow of desires - that enter like rivers into the ocean, which is ever being filled but is always still - can alone achieve peace, and not the man who strives to satisfy such desires.

sutra.meaning: Spiritual ignorance is the root of all suffering because it may cause arrogance, cravings, aversion, attachment etc which are impediments to growth and cause suffering.

sections.insight: Unawareness fuels all reactions which cause karmic residue.
sections.reflectionPrompt: am I unaware of who I really am?
sections.practice: Observe your reactions in all situations specially those that cause you suffering.

sutra.meaning: Confusing temporary as permanent is ignorance for example assuming the world to be prmanent.

sections.insight: Misperception creates suffering. Life itself is impermanent so everything else around it too is not permanent.
sections.reflectionPrompt: What am I holding as permanent which is not so?

sutra.meaning: Ego is identification of seer with seeing ie the body, mind and intellect as the eternal, indestructible Self

sections.insight: We cling to what feels good.
sections.shlokaFrom: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते |आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः || 5.22
sections.wisdomFrom: The pleasures that arise from contact with the sense objects, though appearing as enjoyable to worldly-minded people, are verily a source of misery. O son of Kunti, such pleasures have a beginning and an end, and so the wise do not delight in them.

sections.practice: Face all discomfort with dispassion today.

sutra.meaning: Fear of loss persists even in the wise

sections.insight: Fear is deeply rooted. All fear emanates from the fear of death.
sections.practice: Observe the fears you confront today, no matter how small.

sections.reflectionPrompt: What pattern repeats in my life?
sections.practice: Observe patterns and cycles occuring in your life.

sutra.meaning: Wise see suffering in all change

sections.reflectionPrompt: can I prevent suffering in the future?
sections.shlokaFrom: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते॥ 14.22
sections.wisdomFrom: He who seated like one unconcerned is not moved by the modes of nature, who remains firm and never wavers, knowing that the modes alone are active.

sutra.meaning: Union of seer and seen causes suffering

sections.practice: Observe separation. Observe how it will make you feel.
sections.shlokaFrom: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः।नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां सन्न्यासेनाधिगच्छति॥ 18.49
sections.wisdomFrom: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled - he attains the supreme perfection of freedom from action through renunciation.

sutra.meaning: Desires are beginningless and have existed eternally as the desire to live is eternal.

sections.shlokaFrom: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते।सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते॥ 6.4
sections.wisdomFrom: When one is neither attached to sense objects nor to actions, such a person is said to be elevated in the science of Yog, having renounced all desires for the fruits of actions.

sutra.meaning: Impressions and desires are bound by cause and effect. Removing cause removes effect

sections.practice: Go deeper into your deep desires.
sections.shlokaFrom: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः॥ 3.19
sections.wisdomFrom: Therefore, without attachment, perform always the work that has to be done, for man attains the highest by doing work without attachment.
